title: Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court — Article 11: Jurisdiction ratione temporis
issuing_body: International Criminal Court / Assembly of States Parties
notes: Article 11 governs jurisdiction ratione temporis: the Court's jurisdiction is limited to crimes committed after the Statute entered into force, with the State-specific rule in Article 11(2) and its Article 12(3) declaration exception. This record is a legal-source identity, not a finding that jurisdiction exists in any particular case. Territorial/personal jurisdiction, trigger mechanisms, admissibility, elements, individual responsibility, liability, and guilt require separate analysis.
